paragraphs: I'm a linguist working on LLM evaluation: I build test sets that show where language models fail with real language, and why.

I'm in the second year of an MA in Language, Mind & Technology at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań (cognitive linguistics, psycholinguistics, NLP, Python, R). My thesis examines how LLMs handle non-native English. I design graded test sets of Polish-L1 learner-style messages and measure where output quality drops, and whether tokenization or training data is behind it.
Native Polish, fluent English. Open to LLM evaluation, data annotation, search quality rating, taxonomy and responsible AI roles, remote/async or in Poznań.
about.cv_summary: MA student in Language, Mind & Technology at Adam Mickiewicz University, working at the intersection of linguistics and LLM evaluation. As a volunteer with SpeakLeash, I design Polish-language benchmarks for the Bielik LLM; my MA research examines how NLP models handle non-native English. Native Polish speaker with C1 English and hands-on experience writing precise test items, judging model outputs and analysing results in Python and R

projects.title: Polish LLM Evaluation Test Sets
projects.summary: Designed four 50-item test sets probing Polish language understanding in LLMs: irony comprehension, implicature, case marking vs word order (who did what to whom), and English–Polish false friends. Minimal pairs and short dialogues with closed-format answers, piloted on several models. Sets shared with a SpeakLeash community member for evaluating the Bielik LLM.

projects.title: Lost in Translation
bullets_cv: Collected 50 LLM responses via API; measured cross-lingual consistency with LaBSE embeddings (median cosine .81) and sentiment with XLM-RoBERTa
Tested differences with the Wilcoxon signed-rank test (p = .0004) and reported effect sizes
projects.summary: A Python pipeline comparing a language model's answers to 25 matched English/Polish prompts on Polish history, literature and social norms, with English and Polish Wikipedia as a human-written baseline, LaBSE and XLM-RoBERTa for similarity and sentiment, and Wilcoxon tests. Polish answers were milder in tone, but so is Polish Wikipedia.

publications.title: Echoes of the Mind
publications.description: Echoes of the Mind is a work of literary journalism following Julia, a psychiatrist, through a single 24-hour shift at a psychiatric emergency department in Poland. Through three patient encounters — an elderly man with alcohol-induced delirium, a young man with religious delusions, and a paranoid schizophrenic terrified of technology — the story uses individual cases as a lens for broader social critique, examining Poland’s cultural relationship with alcoholism, the entanglement of the Catholic Church with political life, and the psychological consequences of digitalization.
